398792.note: Record is the Engbers-Galvin conjecture verbatim. Resolved by Gan-Loh-Sudakov, 'Maximizing the number of independent sets of a fixed size' (arXiv:1311.4147; Combin. Probab. Comput. 24 (2015) 521-527), Theorem 1.2, retained and body-checked here: 'Let delta <= n/2. For every t >= 3, every n-vertex graph G with minimum degree at least delta satisfies i_t(G) <= i_t(K_{delta,n-delta}), and when t <= delta, K_{delta,n-delta} is the unique extremal graph.' Sources: arxiv.org/abs/1311.4147; doi 10.1017/S0963548314000546.

400177.note: Does min degree >= n force an immersion of K_n? Open. Best known: min degree >= 11t+7 forces a strong K_t immersion (Dvorak-Yepremyan, 'Complete graph immersions and minimum degree', arXiv:1512.00513, J. Graph Theory 88 (2018) 211-221; abstract verified via public search, PDF not retained). Gap 11n+7 vs n; no small mechanism; complete bipartites K_{n,n} DO contain K_n immersions (round-robin lifts), so no easy counterexample either.

400244.note: Alon's problem resolved. Decisive: 'Quadratic-size Random Permutations are Universal' (arXiv:2610.13530, 2026-10), retained and body-checked: 'We prove that a uniformly random permutation of length 32n^2 is n-universal with probability at least 1-exp(-cn/log n) ... resolves an open problem of Alon' (the paper itself credits the proof to GPT-6 Pro). 32k^2 <= 1000k^2, so f(k) <= 1000k^2 holds. Prior progress: He, 'Universality of random permutations' (arXiv:1911.12878, n = 2000k^2 log log k) and He-Kwan. The record's model (n distinct reals i.i.d. uniform) is a uniformly random n-permutation, matching.

400774.note: Davies' strengthened conjectures: ratio >= 4/3 for all triangle-free G plus alpha/E >= 2-o_d(1) at minimum degree d. Open; the 4/3 core is Davies' Conjecture 1 (see 400775) and the min-degree part is an open Shearer-type refinement. Ramsey-theoretically loaded: per Davies, any constant > 1 would improve the R(3,k) bound. No small mechanism.

400775.note: Verbatim Davies' Conjecture 1 (arXiv:1606.01043, retained and body-checked): 'For every triangle-free graph G, alpha(G)/alpha_G(1) >= 4/3'; author's note: smallest ratio found is 197136/137585 = 1.43283... on the R(3,9)>=36 graph, and any constant > 1 would improve R(3,k). Open since 2016. RUN HERE (bounded, exact): exhaustive labeled triangle-free graphs on n<=7 vertices (2+7+41+388+5789+133501 = 139,728 graphs; scripts/triangle_free_ratio_small_n.py, work/triangle_free_ratio_small_n.out): min alpha/E = 1.466667 (=C5, n=5) and ALL ratios >= 4/3. Finite evidence only; does NOT clear the conjecture. A full-scope proof needs new hard-core/entropy machinery beyond short-proof scale; not briefed.

400776.note: Record is the finite (gamma>0, n>=n_0) form of the theorem of Reiher-Roedl-Rucinski-Schacht-Szemeredi, 'Minimum vertex degree condition for tight Hamiltonian cycles in 3-uniform hypergraphs' (arXiv:1611.03118; Proc. London Math. Soc. 2019), retained and body-checked: 'every 3-uniform hypergraph with n vertices and minimum vertex degree at least (5/9+o(1))C(n,2) contains a tight Hamiltonian cycle', with asymptotically optimal lower-bound constructions. For any fixed gamma>0 the record's (5/9+gamma)n^2/2 >= (5/9+o(1))C(n,2) for all large n, so the record follows.

400796.note: Literal reading: c(d) = min_{K subset L} E V(P^K_{d+1}) / E V(P^L_{d+1}) over convex bodies with no volume normalization. Take K_eps = [0,1]^(d-1)x[0,eps] subset L = [0,1]^d: the slab 0<=x_d<=eps is convex, so the hull of d+1 points of K_eps lies in it and V_d(hull) <= eps * (bounded projection volume), giving E V(P^K_eps) = O(eps) -> 0 while E V(P^L_{d+1}) > 0 is fixed. Hence the literal infimum is 0 (not attained) and no positive lower bound exists: the comparison constant is degenerate without the intended normalization. RUN HERE: numeric illustration work/comparison_constant_thin_demo.out (ratio ~ eps, d=3). No mechanism for the intended version; no brief.

400867.note: The record's concrete question is settled: A(4, arccos(1/3)) = 14, proved by T. S. Tomar, 'Spherical codes with minimal angle arccos(1/3) in dimensions four, five and six' (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23603434, dated 2026-10-23), retained and body-checked: 'We prove A(4, arccos 1/3) = 14, A(5, arccos 1/3) <= 22 and A(6, arccos 1/3) <= 34. The previous upper bounds were 15, 23 and 35.' Certificates are exact rational solutions of the second Lasserre level (de Laat-Leijenhorst formulation), superseding the 16/15 two-/three-point bounds quoted in the record; the 14-point construction was already known.
